title: A transport estimate gives joint continuity
source_anchor: Original Samplinglib path-law transport supplement: A transport estimate gives joint continuity
target_statement: Let \(T\) be a first-countable topological space, \(\Omega\) a measurable space, and \(E\) a compact topological space with a measurable structure for which every open subset of \(E\times E\) is measurable in the product sigma algebra. Let \(P\) be a probability law on \(\Omega\), and let \(X_t:\Omega\to E\) be measurable for every \(t\in T\). Assume that, on one event of full probability, \(t\mapsto X_t\) is continuous on all of \(T\). Write \(\mu_t=(X_t)_\#P\). Let \(c:E\times E\to[0,\infty)\) be a continuous finite cost with \(c(x,x)=0\) for every \(x\). Let \(F\) be a normed additive commutative group, \(U:T\times E\to F\) any field, and \(L\in\mathbb R\). Suppose the bound below holds for every pair \((t,x),(s,y)\). Then \(U\) is jointly continuous. Here \(\Pi(\mu,\nu)\) denotes the probability couplings. The map \(\operatorname{toReal}\) takes the ordinary real value at finite inputs and sends \(\infty\) to zero; the costs \(Q(t,s)\) here are finite by compactness and the explicit same-sample coupling.
